items.title: Eddie Marshall interviewed by Monk Rowe, San Francisco, California, August 8, 2002
items.q: I met Art Taylor and he invited me to go to these sessions.

ctx.x: Oh man, I went to New York, it was terrible. After being such a big cheese in Springfield, Mass you know, I’ll never forget I got off the — well actually I went to New York first without my drums. I stayed with my aunt who lives in Franklin Roosevelt Apartments way on the lower East Side. And she had two kids, I’ll never forget it, and they were just all over me. They thought they were going to have a big brother or something, I was 17, 18 years old. And so I couldn’t do that. I left there. The fact is I went to…

Music. It was a GI bill school. You know it gets kids getting out of the Korean War, they had the GI bill and people were going into music. And it was on 42nd Street. And that’s when I started meeting musicians and getting a little more into it and I met Art Taylor and he invited me to go to these sessions. He used to have these sessions in the East Village that, you know after the gigs ended at three or four in the morning then they’d go to these sessions and play until seven. And I really didn’t really do too…
